question: Which Louisville census tracts have the most property maintenance violations, and what share of adults there get too little sleep?

answer.sql: SELECT t.name AS tract_name,COALESCE(n.n,0) AS louisville_metro_ky_property_maintenance_inspection_violations_count,CAST(h.totalpop18plus AS DOUBLE) AS totalpop18plus,CAST(h.sleep_crudeprev AS DOUBLE) AS sleep_prevalence,t.geoid FROM fw_pg.tracts_21111 t LEFT JOIN fw_pg.tract_counts n ON n.geoid=t.geoid AND n.run_id='r_20261026_f7a20e' AND n.source='m1_city' AND n.grp='all' LEFT JOIN session.fw_f7a20e_m2_cdc h ON h.tractfips=t.geoid ORDER BY louisville_metro_ky_property_maintenance_inspection_violations_count DESC NULLS LAST,tract_name

analysis.reason: Tracts are ranked by raw property-maintenance violation counts to answer 'most'; CDC PLACES already reports the adult insufficient-sleep share per tract, so no cross-tract rate or correlation is needed. CDC prevalence is an adult rate; the accompanying city count is raw workload, not a second health rate.
